title: Cache Stampede

searches.query: "Cache Stampede" interview request coalescing lock expiry
searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: Go x/sync: singleflight
sources.supportRationale: Per-Group duplicate in-flight function suppression; not a distributed ownership primitive.

sources.title: AWS Builders Library: caching challenges and strategies
sources.supportRationale: Measured cache value, modal failure behavior and origin protection.

sources.title: Redis: distributed locks
sources.supportRationale: Lease ownership, safe release and failover limitations; a refresh lease is not a business correctness guarantee.

sources.title: Nishtala et al.: Scaling Memcache at Facebook, NSDI 2013
sources.supportRationale: Original stale-set and lease-based load-control design, scoped to the engineered system described.

sources.title: RFC 5861: HTTP cache-control extensions for stale content
sources.supportRationale: Bounded stale-while-revalidate/stale-if-error semantics, not indefinite permission to reuse data.

sources.title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
sources.supportRationale: Shared/private storage, cache keys, validation and freshness semantics.

sources.title: Microsoft Azure Architecture: cache-aside pattern
sources.supportRationale: Application-owned loading and invalidation order; example ordering does not eliminate every concurrent stale fill.

scenarios.theme: A two-second fill at fifty requests/second creates roughly a hundred loads. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: All callers miss the same scoped view and the origin slows under duplicated work. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cache Stampede to hot key miss.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A two-second fill at fifty requests/second creates roughly a hundred loads. What changes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Coalesce overlapping work per safe key in the needed scope, bound waiters/refresh deadlines and protect aggregate origin capacity

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Waiters add latency/state; a permitted stale view can avoid waiting

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A local coalescer still permits work in other processes, and a unique-key flood needs a separate capacity policy.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to single, strategy; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.assumptions: A warm-up job gave every entry the same deadline; most arriving requests concern different keys. What will you do?

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cache Stampede to synchronized keys.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Spread allowed expiry/refresh times, warm high-value entries gradually and enforce aggregate origin admission

scenarios.theme: A slow refresh owner outlives its lease and overwrites a newer result. What prevents it?
scenarios.assumptions: A second worker acquires the expired lease and publishes version 2 before the first returns version 1. What will you implement?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cache Stampede to expired owner.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A slow refresh owner outlives its lease and overwrites a newer result. What prevents it?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use a verified ownership/version publication guard in its actual atomic coherence boundary and retain/recover the metadata it needs

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Guards add coordination and can reduce availability on unknown state; simpler stale display may fit another requirement

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A cache refresh lease is not a payment idempotency guarantee.

scenarios.theme: Serving stale content keeps latency low during an outage. When must it stop?
scenarios.assumptions: The product allows a limited stale public catalog view, but the current fallback has no age cutoff and also serves private entitlements. What will you change?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cache Stampede to stale refresh bound.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Serving stale content keeps latency low during an outage. When must it stop?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Separate representation policies, enforce the allowed age/visibility boundary and refuse or use a capable authority once it cannot be met

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Stopping stale reuse reduces availability; longer explicitly accepted public staleness is another product decision

scenarios.theme: Bots ask for millions of nonexistent keys. Will negative caching solve everything?
scenarios.assumptions: Each request uses a different ID and the cache fills with low-reuse negatives while origin traffic stays high. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cache Stampede to random missing keys.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Bots ask for millions of nonexistent keys. Will negative caching solve everything?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Bound admission/key cardinality, cache only confirmed absence under a useful scoped short policy and enforce origin/resource limits

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Negative caching helps repeated absent keys, not arbitrary unbounded novelty

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Never store timeout-as-absence or allow the negative set to evict all valuable hot data unchecked.

scenarios.theme: One caller times out and cancels a shared refresh needed by many others. Who owns cancellation?
scenarios.assumptions: A coalescer ties refresh lifetime to the first request’s context. Other active waiters now fail and immediately restart work. What will you choose?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cache Stampede to cancelled waiter.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: One caller times out and cancels a shared refresh needed by many others. Who owns cancellation?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Give shared refresh work an explicit bounded lifetime/owner policy, allow departing waiters to stop waiting independently where appropriate and cap remaini

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Independent work can outlive one request and needs strict resource limits; tightly request-bound work may fit simpler cases

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Never turn cancellation into unbounded background jobs or assume a local coordination primitive supplies the desired lifecycle automatically.
